title: Design System: The Atmospheric Builders' Retreat

display.purpose: The stacked retreat name on the hero; line 1 at clamp(3.4rem, 13.5vw, 6rem), line 2 at clamp(2.55rem, 10vw, 4.5rem). Always uppercase, line-height 0.92. The organizer rail title reuses the atom at a one-off rail scale.

headline.purpose: Question titles ('ARE YOU IN?') and the review title.

title.purpose: Denser interactive items: dates calendar and location ranking. Reused verbatim by the organizer's sign-in gate title (a mini hero).

stat.purpose: The organizer rail's display numerals: the title ramp's endpoints (2.2rem–3.6rem) interpolated on viewport HEIGHT (3.2vh) so the full stat stack fits the first viewport. Tabular numerals, min-width 1.6ch.

place.purpose: Location names on the survey; reused verbatim by the organizer's section titles ('When can they come', 'Responses', 'Allowlist').

body.purpose: Prompts and explanatory copy, 38-46ch measure. The hero acknowledgment scales up to clamp(1rem, 1.6vw + 0.7rem, 1.375rem).

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels, rail section heads, table headers, window rank labels, and the status chip (0.6875rem, 0.18em tracking). KEPT by explicit user decision 2026-08-04 as a documented exception to the craft-floor kicker ban; on /organizer it is labels and section heads only, never an eyebrow — the survey hero's kicker is the sole eyebrow use. Ledger facts use the sibling 0.8125rem / 0.14em style.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The only easing in the world; every transition and the settle use it.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: The one authored motion, survey-only: item content settles upward when it enters (IntersectionObserver threshold 0.4). Gated on html.js; neutralized under prefers-reduced-motion. The organizer has zero entrances.

motion.name: chrome
motion.purpose: Rail stops, progress dots, and the organizer's tally-bar scale.

motion.name: state-micro
motion.purpose: Calendar cells, chips, option rows, switch knob, filter segments, table-row expanders.

components.name: Pill Button
components.description: The single primary action per feed item or section; full-width solid white pill, often carrying the filled Bluesky butterfly.
components.css: .ds-stage { background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; } .ds-pill { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.6rem; width: 100%; min-height: 3.25rem; padding: 0.7rem 1.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; color: #0b0908; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 650; font-size: 1.0625rem; cursor: pointer; transition: transform 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-pill:hover { transform: scale(1.015); } .ds-pill:active { transform: scale(0.985); } .ds-pill:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-pill:disabled { opacity: 0.55; cursor: not-allowed; transform: none; }

components.name: Ledger Rows
components.description: Hairline-ruled label/value fact rows; the world's way of presenting data without boxes — hero facts, stat stacks, best windows, toggle rows.
components.html:
• What3 nights · 2 full days
  • WhereSouthern California
  • WhenSometime between Sept 1 – Nov 15
components.css: .ds-ledger { list-style: none; margin: 0; background: #0b0908; color: #ffffff; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-ledger > li { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 1.125rem; padding: 0.65rem 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); font-size: 0.8125rem; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; font-weight: 500; } .ds-ledger > li:last-child { border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); } .ds-ledger-label { color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); flex: 0 0 auto; } .ds-ledger-value { text-align: right; }

components.name: Choice Option
components.description: Radio choices as ledger rows with a 1.75px ring; selected ring fills white with a punched dot.
components.css: .ds-options { border: none; margin: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-option { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.9rem; padding: 0.95rem 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); cursor: pointer; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); transition: color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-option:last-child { border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); } .ds-option:hover, .ds-option.ds-on { color: #ffffff; } .ds-option input { position: absolute; opacity: 0; width: 1px; height: 1px; } .ds-ring { flex: 0 0 auto; width: 1.15rem; height: 1.15rem; border-radius: 999px; border: 1.75px solid currentColor; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-option.ds-on .ds-ring { background: #ffffff; border-color: #ffffff; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 3px #0b0908; } .ds-option input:focus-visible + .ds-ring { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-option-label { font-size: 1.0625rem; line-height: 1.4; }

components.name: Kicker
components.description: The uppercase label atom — kept by explicit user decision as a documented exception to the craft-floor kicker ban; on /organizer it appears only as field labels and section heads, never as an eyebrow.
components.html: For the builders of the Atmosphere
components.css: .ds-kicker-stage { background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; } .ds-kicker { margin: 0; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Underline Input
components.description: Transparent field with only a bottom hairline; the underline brightens to full white on focus.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.45rem; background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-field-label { font-size: 0.6875rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: 0.18em; text-transform: uppercase; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); } .ds-field-input { background: transparent; border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); border-radius: 0; padding: 0.45rem 0 0.55rem; font: inherit; font-size: 1.125rem; color: #ffffff; } .ds-field-input::placeholder { color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); } .ds-field-input:focus { outline: none; border-bottom-color: #ffffff; }

components.name: Outline Chip
components.description: Pill-shaped outline token for date ranges, half-day toggles, and allowlist handles; selected state inverts to solid white, responded state brightens the border.
components.css: .ds-chips { display: flex; gap: 0.5rem; flex-wrap: wrap; background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-chip { border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); border-radius: 999px; background: transparent; color: #ffffff; font-size: 0.8125rem; padding: 0.4rem 0.85rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: #ffffff; } .ds-chip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-chip-on { background: #ffffff; border-color: #ffffff; color: #0b0908; } .ds-chip-half { background: linear-gradient(to bottom, #ffffff 50%, transparent 50%); border-color: #ffffff; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.9); }

components.name: Segmented Filter
components.description: An outlined 999px group of scope segments; the active segment fills solid ink with ground text. Used for the heatmap's Everyone / Yes-only filter.
components.css: .ds-filter-stage { background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; } .ds-filter { display: inline-flex; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); border-radius: 999px; overflow: hidden; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-filter-btn { padding: 0.35rem 0.9rem; border: none; background: transparent; font-size: 0.8125rem; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), color 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-filter-btn:hover { color: #ffffff; } .ds-filter-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-filter-btn.ds-on { background: #ffffff; color: #0b0908; font-weight: 600; }

components.name: Switch
components.description: The reopen-survey toggle: a 999px outlined track whose checked state inverts the whole control — track fills ink, knob becomes ground and slides right.
components.html:
Reopen survey
Reopen survey (on)
components.css: .ds-switch-stage { background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-toggle-row { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 0.75rem; padding: 0.45rem 0; border-top: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); } .ds-toggle-label { font-size: 0.9375rem; color: #ffffff; } .ds-switch { flex: 0 0 auto; width: 2.6rem; height: 1.5rem; border-radius: 999px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.45); background: transparent; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 0.2rem; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-knob { width: 1rem; height: 1rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; transition: translate 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-switch.ds-checked { background: #ffffff; border-color: #ffffff; } .ds-switch.ds-checked .ds-knob { background: #0b0908; translate: 1.05rem 0; }

components.name: Heatmap Cells
components.description: Availability day cells obeying the Computed Ink Rule: fill alpha = 0.05 + 0.95 × (count / peak), half-day splits via the top/bottom gradient device, numeral flips to ground above 0.5 mean alpha, 0.07 keyline holds zero-count shape.

components.css: .ds-hm-stage { background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; } .ds-hm-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(6, 2.2rem); gap: 3px; font-family: 'Hanken Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif; } .ds-hm-cell { aspect-ratio: 1; min-height: 2rem; display: grid; place-items: center; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.07); color: #ffffff; } .ds-hm-cell.ds-out { border: none; color: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.35); opacity: 0.45; }

components.name: Rail Stop
components.description: A stop on the survey's fixed right-edge glyph rail: 1.75-stroke outline icon, active left dot, filled tick badge when answered.
components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1.15rem; background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; width: fit-content; } .ds-stop { position: relative; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 2.4rem; height: 2.4rem; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; color: #ffffff; opacity: 0.62; transition: opacity 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-stop:hover { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.12); } .ds-stop:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-stop-active { opacity: 1; } .ds-stop-active::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: -0.55rem; top: 50%; translate: 0 -50%; width: 3px; height: 3px; border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; } .ds-tick { position: absolute; right: 0.05rem; top: 0.05rem; display: grid; place-items: center; width: 0.85rem; height: 0.85rem; border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; color: #0b0908; }

components.css: .ds-dots { display: flex; gap: 0.7rem; background: #0b0908; padding: 1.25rem; width: fit-content; } .ds-dot { width: 0.5rem; height: 0.5rem; border: none; border-radius: 999px; background: #ffffff; opacity: 0.35; cursor: pointer; padding: 0; transition: opacity 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-dot:hover { opacity: 0.7; } .ds-dot:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #ffffff; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-dot-on { opacity: 1; transform: scale(1.25); }

narrative.overview:
Every screen is one full-viewport photograph of Southern California at dusk, and the interface is a single voice speaking over it in pure white. The survey refuses the centered-card stepper on a gray ground: it is a feed you flick through, one item per viewport, snap-scrolled like the social product its audience lives in. The photography — real Wikimedia location shots and labeled synthetic desert-modern atmosphere — carries all of the color; the UI contributes exactly one ink.

Density is low and bottom-weighted. Each item breathes at the top and settles its content toward the bottom edge, where a scrim gradient darkens the photograph to near-black so text never negotiates with the image. Structure is drawn, not boxed: hairline rules at 35% white separate ledger rows; the only filled container in the world is the fully-rounded white pill. A film-grain tile at 7% overlay unifies photographic sources into one material.

The world now has a second surface: the organizer room (/organizer) is the same night at Operate density. The photographs stay home — the ground is the solid dusk near-black carrying the same grain at its flat-surface blend — and the one ink does data work: a command rail of condensed display numerals on the left, an availability heatmap whose cells are computed white alpha, hairline ledgers and tables in the content column. It refuses the KPI-card dashboard-on-gray the way the survey refuses the stepper. Density rises; the material does not change.
keyCharacteristics: One UI color: white, stepped only by opacity (100 / 70 / 45 / 35 / 12 — plus 14 and 7 as data-density steps).
Full-bleed photographic grounds under a bottom-heavy scrim on the survey; solid #0b0908 ground on operate surfaces; the grain tile on both.
Ultra-condensed stacked display caps (Big Shoulders) against a quiet grotesk body (Hanken Grotesk).
Hairline ledger rows for facts, options, and data; the white pill as the single filled action.
Two densities, one world: the feed snap-scrolls one item per viewport; the organizer scrolls freely under a sticky command rail.
One authored motion: content settles upward 28px when a feed item snaps in. The organizer has zero entrances.
1.75-stroke outline icon rail; the filled Bluesky butterfly is the lone deliberate outsider.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: The interface owns exactly one color: white. Hierarchy is opacity (70/45/35/14/12/7), never a second hue. If a design needs another color, it comes from a photograph.

rules.name: The Computed Ink Rule
rules.body: When ink encodes data (the availability heatmap), intensity is white alpha computed from the data — 0.05 + 0.95 × (count / peak), floored so a single person stays visible against zero — and the cell numeral flips from ink to ground when the cell's mean alpha exceeds 0.5, so contrast is computed, not blended. Data never gets a color scale; it gets more or less of the one ink.

rules.name: The Scrim Guarantee Rule
rules.body: Text never sits on raw photography. Every feed item carries a bottom-weighted gradient from transparent to 90-98% #0b0908 (a darker variant exists for dense items like the calendar); location cards carry a left-to-right equivalent. Contrast is guaranteed by the scrim, not negotiated per photo. The organizer's flat ground needs no scrim; the guarantee there is the ground itself.

rules.name: The Stacked Caps Rule
rules.body: Display type is always uppercase, always line-height 0.92, and multi-line titles stack as separate spans that may differ in size. Never letter-space display caps beyond 0.005em.

rules.name: The Kicker Exception
rules.body: The uppercase kicker/eyebrow (.kicker) is normally banned by the craft floor, but it is KEPT in this world by explicit user decision (2026-08-04), which overrides the ban. It is a documented exception scoped to this project: use the .kicker atom exactly as defined; do not invent additional eyebrow variants. On /organizer the kicker appears only as field labels and section heads, never as an eyebrow above a heading — the gate's eyebrow was removed per the craft floor, and the survey hero's kicker remains the sole eyebrow use in the world.

rules.name: The One Viewport Rule
rules.body: One feed item owns the entire viewport. Nothing scrolls inside an item on the feed axis; if content grows, it earns density (the darker scrim), never a second screen. This rule is scoped to the survey feed: the organizer is the world's one freely-scrolling surface — Operate density earns a normal document scroll under the sticky command rail.

rules.name: The Flat World Rule
rules.body: No drop shadows, ever. Layering is expressed with scrims, hairlines, backdrop blur, and opacity — never with a shadow vocabulary.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: Every ground carries the grain tile (/media/grain.png, background-size: 340px), blended per surface: photographic grounds at opacity: 0.07; mix-blend-mode: overlay; flat #0b0908 grounds at opacity: 0.05; mix-blend-mode: screen. Overlay needs photographic midtones beneath it and vanishes on near-black; screen at the lower opacity is the same grain made visible on a solid ground. Never omit the grain, and never use any other opacity/blend pair.

rules.name: The One Container Rule
rules.body: The fully-rounded white pill is the only filled container in the interface. Round controls (chips, filter segments, the switch) may invert to solid ink in their selected state — that reads as state, not surface. Text content is never boxed or carded; it sits directly on the ground, structured by hairlines.

rules.name: The One Settle Rule
rules.body: The caption settle is the only authored entrance in the world. New components may transition state (opacity, transform, ≤0.45s, --ease-out) but never add a second choreographed entrance. The organizer surface holds this at zero: nothing on it animates in.

rules.name: The Butterfly Exception
rules.body: The Bluesky butterfly is a filled brand mark, deliberately outside the 1.75-stroke system — it is a wordmark, not an icon. No other filled glyph is permitted.

dos: Do put every surface on the dusk ground — full-bleed photography with the scrim on the survey, solid #0b0908 on operate surfaces — always with the grain tile at its surface's blend (0.07 overlay on photographs, 0.05 screen on flat ground).
Do express all hierarchy as white opacity steps: 1 / 0.7 / 0.45 / 0.35 / 0.12, plus the two data-density steps (0.14 row separators, 0.07 cell keylines) on dense data surfaces — no other alphas.

Do set display type in Big Shoulders, 700 (650 for the place/section ramp), uppercase, line-height: 0.92, sized with the established clamps — including the height-interpolated Stat ramp for rail numerals.
Do structure data as hairline ledgers and tables (1px solid var(--ink-35), 0.14 inside dense tables) and reserve the solid white pill for the single primary action per item or section.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion, env(safe-area-inset-*), and the html.js gate on anything that starts hidden.
donts: Don't introduce a second UI color, a gray ramp, or tinted surfaces — even data visualization is computed white alpha, never a color scale.
Don't use box-shadows, filled cards, or bordered boxes around text; the pill is the only filled container, and KPI cards are refused on the organizer.
Don't add icons outside the 1.75-stroke/round-join/24-grid system, and don't fill any glyph except the Bluesky butterfly.
Don't author new entrance animations; the snap-in settle is the world's one moment, and the organizer proves screens work with none.
Don't let text sit on unscrimmed photography, shrink the gutter/rail clearance (--gutter + 2.4rem right on the feed), or use the kicker as an eyebrow anywhere except the survey hero.
